pi.hero.lede: This page points you to the right information for your symptom — it does not diagnose. Diagnosis comes only from a doctor's examination.
pi.rt.title: Which of these matches your problem?
pi.rt.lede: The cards below only lead you to the right information page — this is not a diagnosis.
pi.rt.1.d: Piles (haemorrhoids) are the best-known cause, but bleeding can have several other causes too — read the full page.
pi.rt.2.d: A sharp or burning pain is a typical sign of an anal fissure — read the full page.
pi.rt.3.d: Repeated pus or discharge near the anus can be a sign of an anal fistula — read the full page.
pi.rt.4.d: Constipation, itching or small skin lumps — the education guide below covers these.
pi.rt.noteGrid: Remember: the same symptom can belong to several conditions. This list only shows the way — a doctor's examination is the only reliable way to know the cause.
pi.gd.title: Other related conditions
pi.gd.lede: Beyond piles, fissure and fistula — a basic idea of some other conditions that affect the anal area, for learning.
pi.gd.pn.p: A pilonidal sinus is a small hole or tunnel in the skin at the top of the buttocks, in the cleft between them. When hairs are pushed under the skin by pressure and friction, irritation can follow; if it becomes infected, a painful, pus-filled abscess can develop quickly, making sitting difficult. Many people do not notice it until infection develops.
pi.gd.pn.b1: Early on there may be no symptoms at all — just a small dimple or pit in the skin
pi.gd.pn.b2: With infection: pain and swelling at the top of the cleft over a few days — sitting becomes painful
pi.gd.pn.b3: Pus or blood draining from the area, sometimes with a foul smell
pi.gd.pn.b4: Some people also get a mild fever
pi.gd.pn.b5: Washing the area daily, keeping it dry, and avoiding very long periods of sitting — these habits often help
pi.gd.st.p: Anal skin tags are small, soft flaps of excess skin around the anus — often left behind after a swollen pile settles or a fissure heals. They are usually harmless, but any lump around the anus should first be identified by a doctor — other conditions can look very similar, and each is managed differently.
pi.gd.st.b1: Usually painless; friction can cause irritation or itching
pi.gd.st.b2: Difficulty keeping the area clean is a common complaint
pi.gd.st.b3: Piles are red or purple and can bleed; warts are rough-surfaced and can spread — so identification matters
pi.gd.st.b4: Never cut or tie off a tag yourself — pharmacy tag-removers can burn this thin skin and cause infection
pi.gd.st.b5: If removal is ever needed, it is only done as a doctor-performed procedure — often doctors advise leaving them alone
pi.gd.st.b6: If the cause — straining or an untreated fissure — continues, tags can come back
pi.gd.cn.p: Passing stool less often than usual, or hard, dry stool that is difficult to push out — that is constipation. Straining and hard stools are leading drivers of piles, fissures and skin tags, so bringing constipation under control is often part of treating those conditions.
pi.gd.cn.b1: Fewer than three bowel movements a week, or a feeling that the bowel has not emptied
pi.gd.cn.b2: Increase fibre-rich foods gradually — fruits, vegetables, leafy greens
pi.gd.cn.b3: Enough fluids through the day — fibre works together with water
pi.gd.cn.b4: Do not delay the urge; do not sit straining on the toilet for long
pi.gd.cn.b5: A small stool under the feet, knees above hips, makes passing stool easier
pi.gd.cn.b6: Long-standing constipation or blood in the stool — see a doctor instead of self-medicating again and again
pi.gd.note: This information is for learning — what treatment is right for you, your doctor will tell only after an examination.
pi.fv.title: What helps before the first visit
pi.fv.lede: Bringing a few things makes the consultation more useful.
pi.fv.bring.b1: Previous prescriptions or reports — if you have any
pi.fv.bring.b2: A list of the medicines you are taking now — even ones bought from a pharmacy
pi.fv.bring.b3: A short list of the questions you want to ask
pi.fv.what.b1: Your problem is heard in a private, confidential setting
pi.fv.what.b3: The condition is explained and a treatment plan is shared
pi.fv.priv: What you say, the examination and the treatment — all stay confidential. Women and men alike are seen in a dignified, comfortable environment.
pi.col.title: Don't fear colonoscopy — don't self-treat
pi.col.p: At the mere mention of colonoscopy, many avoid the doctor and turn to pharmacy medicines. The clinic's education post warns about this directly — self-treating raises the risk of the disease becoming complicated. If you have symptoms, examination is the first step.

pi.col.cap: A healthy diet supports recovery — from the clinic's education posts
pi.cta.t: Unsure about your symptoms? Call and ask
pi.cta.d: If you cannot tell which page fits you, just call directly — describe the problem and learn the next step.
